crash.title: Crash reports
crash.notBuilt: This build of jojo was made without crash reporting or usage analytics, so nothing is recorded and there is nothing to turn on.
crash.what: When something breaks, jojo can keep the error so you can read it back — useful when the thing that failed has already gone. A report holds the error message, where in jojo it happened, and the stack trace. It never holds your applications, documents, notes, profile or conversations, and API keys, addresses and email addresses are stripped out before a report is written.
crash.where: Reports are kept on this phone, and also sent to Firebase Crashlytics, which adds your device model, its OS version, and a random id used to count how many people hit the same crash. Google keeps those for 90 days. None of your records go with them.
crash.reportHint: On, so a crash you hit is one we can see. Turn it off and nothing is recorded.
crash.usageHint: Counts only, from a fixed list — never what is in your records.
crash.usageDetail: It can only say things from a fixed list — which screen was opened, that an application was added, roughly how many there are. It cannot name an employer, a role, a file or anything you typed. Goes to Google Analytics. With this off, jojo also turns off the screen views and session counts Firebase would otherwise collect on its own.
crash.nothingBroken: Nothing has broken since you turned this on.

errorBoundary.noMessage: No message was attached to the error.
errorBoundary.hint: If it breaks again, close jojo from the app switcher and reopen it.

reporting.title: Crash reports and usage
reporting.description: Two separate things, both on. Turn off either one here or later in Settings. Neither can carry your records: not an application, a document, a note, a profile or a conversation.
reporting.inReport: What is in a crash report

in.message: · The error message and where in jojo it happened.
in.stack: · The stack trace, which names the code that failed.
in.device: · Your device model, its OS version, and a random id used to count how many people hit the same crash — no name, no account.

notIn.records: · Your applications, documents, notes, profile or conversations.
notIn.secrets: · Your API keys, the addresses you use, or any email address — stripped out before a report is written, not before it is sent.

reporting.crashHint: The error and where it happened. Goes to Firebase Crashlytics.
reporting.usageHint: Counts only — which screens are opened, how often. Never what is in them.
reporting.usageDetail: The second one is the only thing jojo sends about what you DO, and it can only ever say things from a fixed list — “the vault was opened”, “an application was added”, “there are 6–20 of them”. It cannot name an employer, a role, a file or anything you typed, because those words are not in the list. Turning it off also stops the screen views Firebase would otherwise collect on its own.
reporting.later: Both are under Settings whenever you want to change them, and turning one off discards what it kept.

working.title: What is working

welcome.title: A tour of jojo, hands on
welcome.body: It points at the real screens and asks you to try each thing as you go. It never types, saves or changes anything for you. Close it whenever you like — your place is kept, and How to use will pick it up again.

today.title: Today
today.body: What is owed now: what is overdue, what is due, and the decisions waiting on you. The screen to open first.

applications.title: Your applications
applications.body: One record per job: the employer, the role, its stage and your notes. Its dates, documents and conversations all hang off it, so nothing is typed twice.

layout.title: A list or a board
layout.body: The same records, two ways. The list sorts and searches; the board shows the stages as columns.

records.title: Six stages
records.body: Draft, Submitted, Screening call, Interview, Offer, Closed. On the board, press and hold a card, then drag it to its next column; each card also has a stage menu. Every move can be undone.

search.title: Search everything
search.body: Applications, reminders and calendar entries, from any tab.

searchScreen.title: Type to find anything
searchScreen.body: A role, an employer or a stage. Tap a result to open it, or go back when you are done looking.

new.title: Make anything
new.body: The + makes an application, a reminder, a calendar entry, a drafted message, a saved link or a saved posting. Nothing is saved until you save, and closing a half-filled form costs nothing.

calendar.title: Every date in one place
calendar.body: Deadlines, interviews and follow-ups are one kind of record, so one entry shows on the calendar, on Today and on its application.

vault.title: The vault
vault.body: Everything that is not an application: reminders, links, files, the snippets you paste into every form, the people you know, and a calculator.

vaultTools.title: One tool at a time
vaultTools.body: Each of these is its own list, and a keyword means the same thing in all of them.

files.title: Files, kept on the phone
files.body: A CV, a statement, a posting — copied into jojo’s own folder, so they survive the original being moved. Tap one to read it here; file it under as many applications as it belongs to.

more.title: More
more.body: Everything else: Job scout, Statistics, the graph, Transfer, your profile, the assistant, Settings and this guide.

scout.title: Job scout
scout.body: Saved searches that watch job boards for you.

scoutScreen.title: Pipelines and suggestions
scoutScreen.body: Each pipeline is a search on a board, run on a schedule or when you ask. What it finds waits as a suggestion you approve or discard, and an approved one becomes a draft application.

statistics.title: Statistics
statistics.body: How your search is going, counted from your own records.

statisticsScreen.title: Rates, with honest ranges
statisticsScreen.body: Response and interview rates, a funnel and what to work on next — each rate with the range it could really be, since a handful of applications is a small sample.

graph.title: The knowledge graph
graph.body: Every record — applications, employers, people, dates, files — drawn as the network it is.

graphScreen.title: Everything, connected
graphScreen.body: Tap a node to see what it connects to, and ask a question to light up the records that match.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.body: Chat with jojo: it finds, adds and updates your records with the app’s own tools, and asks before it changes anything. Until a model is connected it shows worked examples.

transfer.title: Phone and computer
transfer.body: Transfer moves everything between this phone and jojo on your computer over your local network, without going through anyone else.

device.title: Your records live on this phone
device.body: Written straight to the phone’s own storage as you work — no account, no sync, nothing uploaded. Export a copy, or Transfer it to your computer.

model.title: Connect a model
model.body: Where the assistant’s model runs. A server on your own machine — vLLM, Ollama or LM Studio — takes its address and keeps your records on your devices. OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude) and the other cloud providers take an API key. Test connection checks it before anything is saved.

reader.title: Let it read your documents
reader.body: The phone reads Word files, decks, saved pages and text on its own. PDFs need MarkItDown on your computer: start it with the two commands above, then Test connection.

done.title: That’s the tour
done.body: Every change can be undone, and How to use, under More, covers every screen in turn. The tour is there to take again.
